title: Develop IT compliance, risk, and security strategy
goal: The venture has one written register of its IT risks and the rules it must meet, each with an owner, a tolerance the founder set and a mitigation, and every rule names the evidence that would show it is met.

steps.do: List the rules that actually bind this venture's systems, from the obligations record, the markets and industries it operates in and each provider's own terms, and write for each one what it requires of IT and the page and date you read it; name as unknown anything you cannot source and send it to the founder and counsel.

Ask the founder what the venture can actually live with for each kind of loss (hours without a system, records lost, a customer's data exposed, a credential leaked) and write the answers as numbers rather than as adjectives.

Turn those answers into the lines IT works to (the longest outage accepted per system, the oldest acceptable backup, the accounts that must be on MFA with no exception) and record each line on the connection it governs.

Give every risk in the register one owner who can actually act on it, taking the owner from the delegation and the element owners rather than inventing a role, and name each risk whose owner would have to be the founder.

Write who does what in IT risk here (the IT agent identifies, records and narrows; the product lead orders the fixes; the founder accepts a risk or widens access) and say which of these roles nobody holds yet.

consider.why: Separate risk roles only mean something once more than one person or lead is involved.
consider.when: The venture has more than one person, or a lead other than the founder holds a grant over IT.

steps.do: For each binding rule, write the one objective that would satisfy it in this venture's size, and the evidence that would show it met (a dated access review, an export of the records, a signed term), so nothing is claimed without evidence.
Say which existing system or record holds each piece of that evidence, and name every objective whose evidence has nowhere to live, without buying anything to fix it.

Write the register itself: one row per risk with what could happen, how it would happen, which connection and which record it would reach, how likely and how bad, and what evidence the estimate rests on, following ISO 31000's order of identify, analyze and evaluate.
For each risk, say what the venture could still do while it was happening and how long that would last, and mark the risks that would stop the venture completely.

For each risk, write the mitigation and whether it avoids, reduces, transfers or accepts the risk, map it to the control it belongs to in a framework the venture has chosen (NIST Cybersecurity Framework or ISO/IEC 27001, whichever the founder picked, and name the choice if neither), and note any system that also controls physical equipment so its risks are not treated as ordinary software risks.

Record the register, the tolerances and the mitigations as evidence on the decisions they bear on, and raise for the founder each risk whose only answer is to accept it, to spend money, to accept new terms or to widen access, and for the product lead the order of the fixes.

done_criteria.check: Does every risk have one owner who can act on it and a mitigation, did the founder set the tolerance numbers, and does every binding rule cite where it was read and name the evidence that would show it met?
